title: StatusPicker
wrapsNative: A Button trigger and a popover of Buttons grouped under category headings, each icon in its category's colour (a system Menu draws every icon in the tint); Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) and a Section per category remains the choice for the system menu
summary: Shows and changes the workflow status of an issue, task or ticket, with the team's own status names grouped under five fixed categories, using the standard menu picker. Monarch ships no type.
whenToUse: In issue rows, cards and detail screens where the status can be changed. Group statuses by category with a Section and give each category its own SF Symbol, as in the examples, so the status never depends on colour.
whenNotToUse: For a read-only status, show the Label without a menu, or use MonarchStatusBadge. For moving through the linear steps of a form, use MonarchStepper. For urgency, use the priority-picker entry.
api: Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<SelectionValue>, content: () -> Content)
func pickerStyle(_ style: MenuPickerStyle) -> some View

states.name: selected
states.description: The menu shows a checkmark next to the current status; the trigger shows its name (and, in the Menu form, its category symbol in the category colour).

states.name: no status
states.description: Use an optional selection with a "No status" row tagged nil, as the web's none message does.

appearance: System menu in every theme. In the Menu form the trigger takes the Monarch button style and the symbol takes the category's theme role, as on the web: the subtle text colour for backlog and cancelled, the muted text colour for not started, the strong warning colour for in progress and the strong success colour for completed. Inside the system menu the symbols take the menu's own colour, so the symbol shape and the name carry the status.
platformNotes: The web ships StatusPicker on DropdownMenu with drawn glyphs (dashed ring, ring, half-filled ring, check, cross), and Android builds MonarchStatusPicker. On iOS the standard menu picker gives the menu, the category sections, the checkmark, hardware keyboard and VoiceOver behaviour, so Monarch ships no type. A system menu shows SF Symbols, not custom drawings, so the categories use circle.dashed, circle, circle.righthalf.filled, checkmark.circle.fill and xmark.circle.fill. The web's STATUS_CATEGORIES order is the order of the Category enum in the examples; its StatusGlyph for read-only displays is a Label with the same symbol and colour. The web's sm and md sizes map to the Monarch button sizes on the Menu trigger; the glyph-only trigger is the symbol with monarchMinimumHitTarget().
accessibility: System behaviour: the picker is read as a pop-up button with the current status as its value; menu items are read by name under their section, with the selected one marked.
In the Menu form, accessibilityLabel("Status: In progress") names the trigger with the current status, as the web does; a glyph-only trigger keeps that name.
Every category has its own symbol shape and every status its own name, so the status never depends on colour.
A glyph-only trigger needs monarchMinimumHitTarget() for a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: A category with no statuses is skipped, so no empty section appears.
A long status name wraps in the Menu trigger at large text sizes; the system menu truncates as it does for any item.
Section titles inside a menu picker are drawn by the system; on some iOS versions a menu shows sections as separators only, and the symbols still group the statuses.
